page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-16-lssd is an x86_64 virtual instance configured with 16 vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor, providing two threads per core. The instance provides 128 GB of system memory, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a dedicated 402 GB NVMe local solid-state drive. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration features like VAES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark data demonstrates balanced compute and transactional performance across standard enterprise workloads. Single-core execution reflects solid results, scoring 2865.37 in stress-ng tests and 1874.0 in Geekbench, while multi-core workloads yield a Geekbench score of 10103.0 and a PassMark CPU rating of 24412.28. In-memory data structures perform solidly, with Redis SET operations sustaining 20.8 million operations per second and PassMark database operations reaching 6892.5. However, while cached memory reads measure 1132.73 GB/sec, uncached write bandwidth falls significantly to 13.16 GB/sec on large 256 MB block transfers.

The qualitative efficiency profile centers on high memory density and integrated local high-speed storage without requiring attached network volumes. Tradeoffs involve low uncached write throughput and modest processing speeds on large language model prompt evaluations, where 70B parameter models drop to 4.12 tokens per second. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, making it specifically suited for memory-intensive caching tiers, local NVMe scratch databases, static web serving delivering up to 14.4 GB/sec, and intermediate data processing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-16-lssd provides 16 vCPUs and 8 physical cores via an AMD EPYC 9B14 x86_64 processor, paired with 128 GB of memory and an integrated 402 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating at an 8 GB per vCPU memory allocation, it includes AVX-512 vector support and hardware cryptographic extensions. Benchmarks indicate balanced multi-core performance, achieving 20.8 million Redis SET operations per second, a PassMark CPU score of 24412.28, and a static web serving throughput of 14.4 GB/sec. Large-block uncached memory writes present an architectural bottleneck at 13.16 GB/sec, and execution of large 70B language models is limited. With its bundled high-speed local disk and high memory density, this server is suitable for caching deployments, in-memory databases, and high-throughput web services.
